records.text: Model-building guidance given to the user covered defining the cancer type, imaging modality, task, and metrics; obtaining diverse annotated data; choosing a framework and architecture; training with separate training, validation, and test sets; evaluating with task-appropriate measures; interpretability; external or clinical validation; and privacy, bias, fairness, and regulatory concerns. Suggested frameworks included TensorFlow, PyTorch, Keras, and MATLAB; architectures included CNNs, transfer-learned VGG or ResNet, U-Net, FCN, and SegNet.

Preprocessing techniques discussed with the user included format conversion, resizing, intensity normalization, noise reduction, artifact removal, image registration, and ROI segmentation. Suggested augmentations included rotation, flipping, scaling, translation, contrast adjustment, noise injection, elastic deformation, color/brightness jitter, mixup, and random cropping. Tools named included OpenCV, scikit-image, torchvision, Albumentations, imgaug, and Augmentor.

The assistant distinguished simple systems (a single tank) from complex systems (multiple tanks and pumps).

The assistant said greywater-system maintenance may include regular checks for leaks, clogs, and odors; cleaning or replacing filters every 1–3 months; checking tanks for sediment, corrosion, or leaks; monitoring disinfectant levels; maintaining pumps; and removing sludge or sediment every 1–5 years, depending on use.

On 2023-04-25, the assistant gave rough greywater-system installation estimates in US dollars: simple systems, $4,000–$9,000 total; moderate systems, $9,000–$18,000; and complex systems, $18,000–$35,000.
